title: AEM electrolyzer OER reference family
objective: Optional literature-backed electrocatalyst family for alkaline and anion-exchange-membrane electrolyzer anodes. These candidates compare scalable NiFe routes with more architecture-sensitive amorphous variants using alkaline stack defaults rather than PEM materials.

balanced.label: Balanced
balanced.description: Balance current stack economics, evidence quality, route maturity, and reported performance.

cost-first.label: Cost-first
cost-first.description: Bias ranking toward current electrode cost while preserving route and evidence guardrails.

evidence-first.label: Evidence-first
evidence-first.description: Reward stronger literature support and more reproducible alkaline-electrolyzer routes.

route_templates.name: NiFe-LDH alkaline anode route
route_templates.manufacturing_mode: Alkaline or AEM electrolyzer anode coating route
preprocess: Nickel felt or porous transport substrate preparation
route_templates.route_note: Most transferable non-noble alkaline-electrolyzer anode route in the family.

route_templates.name: Seed-assisted NiFe route
route_templates.route_note: Higher-performing structured NiFe route, but seed-layer control and deposition reproducibility reduce maturity versus the plain LDH baseline.

route_templates.name: Cr-doped amorphous NiFe route
route_templates.route_note: Robust-performance route, but dopant control and amorphous-state retention make it less reproducible than the simpler NiFe baselines.

candidates.title: NiFe-LDH scalable anode
candidates.summary: Scalable all-earth-abundant NiFe layered-double-hydroxide route for alkaline or AEM electrolyzer anodes.
decision_notes: Best starting point when the goal is a non-noble alkaline-electrolyzer anode with a credible scale-up story.
Economics stay favorable because the active phase avoids PGMs and the stack defaults use alkaline materials rather than PEM inputs.

pricing.note: NiFe hydroxide catalyst cost held on a derived screening proxy using nickel and iron commodity exposure plus alkaline-anode processing overhead.

candidates.title: Seed-assisted NiFe anode
candidates.summary: Seed-directed NiFe route targeting higher current density and better catalyst utilization in AEM water electrolysis.
decision_notes: Use this when higher anode efficiency is worth tighter deposition control.
The route improves performance but gives up some simplicity relative to the plain NiFe-LDH baseline.

pricing.note: Seed-directed NiFe catalyst held on a derived screening proxy that adds structured-growth overhead to a nickel-iron catalyst basis.

candidates.title: Cr-doped amorphous NiFe route
candidates.summary: Chromium-doped amorphous NiFe route emphasizing robust alkaline OER operation and long-hold stability.
decision_notes: Good fit when alkaline durability matters more than the lowest route complexity.
Chromium-doping and amorphous-state control raise route overhead relative to the simpler NiFe cases.

pricing.note: Chromium-doped amorphous NiFe catalyst cost held on a derived proxy that includes dopant handling and alkaline-anode processing overhead.

candidates.title: NiCo2O4 spinel anode
candidates.summary: Co-precipitated nickel cobaltite spinel: the cobalt-based PGM-free anode axis, running alkaline OER at 1.65 V full-cell for 10 mA/cm2 with commodity-oxide manufacturing.
decision_notes: Adds the cobalt raw-material axis to a family that is otherwise all NiFe - the screen now prices Fe-vs-Co sensitivity directly.

pricing.note: Contained-nickel basis of the NiCo2O4 stoichiometry.
Contained-cobalt basis of the NiCo2O4 stoichiometry; the cost-dominant term.
